title: What You Get for the Price With Storyworth
summary: Every plan includes at least one hardcover book, an audiobook, e-book and our other products. What is inside each Storyworth plan, and the costs people forget to compare.
body_markdown:
Guided memoir services look similar from the outside. A question arrives, somebody answers it, a book turns up at the end of the year. The prices look similar too.


What differs is what is inside the price, and that is hard to see until you have already bought one. Here is what a Storyworth plan includes, laid out so you can compare it against other family storytelling services.


## Everything in this section comes with every plan


Not the most expensive plan. Every plan, including our entry plan.


- A year of weekly questions, sent by email or text
- Answer in writing, by replying to the email or on the site
- Answer out loud by phone, with word-for-word transcription
- Unlimited stories and unlimited photos, with captions
- A library of more than 500 prompts, or write your own
- A hardcover book at the end of the year
- A downloadable e-book of the finished memoir
- A downloadable audiobook of the finished memoir
- Celebrations, Family Newsletters and Journals, at no extra cost, while your plan is active
- A 30-day money-back guarantee
- Printing in the USA with free domestic shipping


The audiobook and e-book are what people are most surprised by. It is not an upsell on a premium tier. A storyteller on the least expensive plan still ends the year with their memoir in a form you can listen to or read on any e-reader. Many services charge up to $50 to download a simple .pdf version of a memoir.


The other products are the second surprise. A Storyworth plan is not only a memoir. While it is active you can also create a Celebration book for a milestone birthday, enjoy a monthly Family Newsletter, or reflect daily with Journals, without paying again.


## What the plans actually cost


We offer three plans in order to make storytelling accessable to everyone. The biggest differences between them is around books and feature access.


- **Basic, $69.** One hardcover book credit up to 480 pages, black and white interior, custom color cover. Story Calls for sharing over the phone.
- **Color, $99.** One hardcover book credit up to 300 pages, full color interior, custom color cover. All three voice methods: Story Calls, Magic Interviews and Family Calls. Personalized questions created for your storyteller plus a built-in proofreader.
- **Unlimited, $199 for the first year, renewing at $99.** Two full color book credits. The ability to give Memoirs to as many people as you want while your subscription is active, so one plan can cover both parents and a discount on extra book credits. Plus everything in the Color plan.


Extra copies can be ordered at any time: $39 for a black and white interior up to 480 pages, $79 for full color up to 300 pages, $99 for full color up to 480 pages.


## The costs people forget to compare


Price per plan is the easy comparison. These are the ones that change the real number.


**Extra copies.** A memoir written by a grandmother with four children may require five book copies, not one. Whether extra copies are available, what they cost, and whether you can order one in five years are three separate questions.


**What happens when the plan ends.** With Storyworth you keep access to your account after the plan is over. You can still edit existing stories, add to them, and print new copies. A service where the stories become unreachable when you stop paying is selling you a subscription, not a book.


**Whether voice costs extra.** Answering by phone is included at every level here. On some services recording is a separate product or a higher tier.


**Whether a second storyteller means a second subscription.** This is the largest hidden difference between services, and it only shows up when you decide you want your father’s stories too.


## How to compare this against anything else


Remento, Memorygram, StoryTerrace, Storii, My Life in a Book, Meminto, MyStories and Memowrite all sell a version of a year of storytelling. The prices are close enough that the inclusions decide it.


Six questions get you a real comparison rather than a sticker price:


1. **What is the book?** Hardcover or softcover, how many pages, is the interior color, and who designed the layout.
2. **How many copies come with the plan, and what does another cost?**
3. **Is there an audiobook or an e-book, and is it extra?**
4. **Can the storyteller answer by phone, and does that cost more?**
5. **What other hidden costs are there?**
6. **Can one plan cover more than one storyteller?**
7. **What happens to the stories when the subscription ends?**


Storyworth’s answers to all seven are above. Ask the same seven of whatever else is on your list, and the gap between the sticker price and the real price usually shows up in questions two, three and seven.


## The short version


The sticker price is the least useful number in this category. What matters is how much of the thing you actually wanted, a finished book your family can keep and reread, is inside the price, and how much of it arrives later as an extra.


Worth doing that arithmetic on every service you are considering, including this one.
